changes.why: (from follow, 25 Nov 2026). The best-run business here, but growth has stalled for two years and the price needs about {need:Kirloskar Pneumatic|18}% a year against my ~15%; a strong second half would bring it back to follow.

I expect about 12% a year of earnings growth against the {need:Medi Assist Healthcare|12}% the price needs ({label:Medi Assist Healthcare|fits}), but the reported P/E is flattered by a one-off tax credit and growth has stalled. I would buy once revenue growth is back near 10% with a margin of 21% or more.

I expect about 25% a year of earnings growth against the {need:Sahajanand Medical Technologies|29}% the price needs ({label:Sahajanand Medical Technologies|full}); worth owning lower, once its own products grow faster again.
The business is on track, but the price now asks for more growth than I expect (moved from own on 22 Nov 2026).
Very profitable and cash-rich, and the price asks for little, but profit is falling and promises keep slipping; I want Q4 to show the margin back at 35–40% (moved from own on 22 Nov 2026).

I expect about 15% a year of earnings growth against the {need:Viviana Power Tech|8}% the price needs ({label:Viviana Power Tech|fits}), but the growth has never produced cash, the balance sheet needs new equity and the related-party dealings are unresolved.

I expect about 12% a year of earnings growth against the {need:MMP Industries|15}% the price needs ({label:MMP Industries|full}); I want the PGCIL insulator approval and the wire-rod plant running first.

The new plant is filling, but I expect about 16% a year of earnings growth against the {need:Bansal Wire Industries|18}% the price needs, and the cash and related-party questions should be answered first.

I expect about 12% a year of earnings growth, close to the {need:Fidel Softech|12}% the price needs, but almost all of it would come from buying Softenger; I want the deal closed and the core business growing again first.

I expect about 25% a year of earnings growth, less than the {need:Sigma Advanced Systems|31}% the price needs ({label:Sigma Advanced Systems|stretched}), and cash is going the wrong way while the next ₹3,000cr raise and deals are still unknown.
Real, owned technology, but profit is not arriving as cash, and the price needs about {need:Tonbo Imaging|33}% a year of earnings growth against my ~18%.

I expect earnings per share to grow about 26% a year to FY30, counted from about ₹7.9cr of normal yearly profit (not the ₹4.3cr left after last year's write-backs) and within management's plan of 30–50% sales growth; the price needs about {need:Innomet Advanced Materials|33}% a year, and five years of cash have not matched the profit. I would look again once H2 FY27 turns the stock build into cash.
I expect about 22% a year of earnings growth, more than the {need:Vivid Electromech|17}% the price needs, but I want to see cash collected before trusting it.
A specialist in a bad year; the price now asks for a little more than a flat FY27 supports (moved from own, 6 Nov 2026).
, in small size. The margin rose as I wanted and the price fits the higher growth now guided.
A real turnaround at a price that now fits; I would own it once the promoter payments are explained.
, in small size. Q2 showed the Q1 profit repeats and debt stopped outrunning revenue, and the price fits my estimate; GPU rents are the risk.
A clever, asset-light brand, but growth is being bought and profit is not turning into cash; wait for a year of positive free cash with the margin holding.
A mid-sized, low-return Morbi tile maker whose earnings depend on gas prices, at about 34 times earnings, a richer price than Somany or Orient Bell for weaker returns.
A cheap, high-return brand, but it must show the margin back above 23% and customer dues falling toward 120 days before I would buy.
A well-spread, well-run chemical maker, but the price already assumes this year's guidance is met; I want to see margins after the Q1 windfall fades.
A good small business at a fair 33 times earnings, but I want to see the new plant running and holding the margin before buying.
Loss-making in three of the last four quarters, stock takes 309 days to sell and free cash over FY22–FY26 was −₹212cr; until it is back in profit with cash following, there is nothing to value.
The price asks for little growth, but I want H2 FY27 to show the promised 20% and cash to follow profit before buying.
Cheap with a strong cash pile, but I want to see the margin back near 24%, the promoter guarantee released and Pearson's share falling before buying.
A real and growing business, but the price already assumes the risky GPU deal works, and the deal's obligations dwarf the company's ₹544cr net worth.
A sound low-cost model, but about 16 times EBITDA is a full price for 11% returns on capital and a debt-funded build-out; wait for the North to turn profitable and costs to fall.
Fast growth, but it is funded with borrowed money and unpaid bills; the price leaves no room for that risk.

A good, cash-generating niche business at about 25 times earnings, but too dependent on a few clients and too new as a listed company; I want the second-half export orders and new wins to show up first.
The low price reflects profit that has not turned into cash, revenue booked on its own project, and heavy dependence on two state customers.
A real, growing rent business at a sensible price after a 24% fall from the IPO price, but wait to see reported profit and how Blackstone exits.
Too much costly debt for a business whose sales have stalled; the handover profits that could fix it are an FY28–FY29 story, and FY27 net debt is guided flat.
A real whisky brand, but the auditor resigned in April 2026 and a group sugar company owed it ₹43cr; at 39 times earnings, governance questions like these rule it out until they are settled.
Cheap at 14 times earnings, but I want to see the doubled plant run full and debt fall in H2 before trusting a commodity business this leveraged.
A fine dairy brand, but the price assumes many years of near-perfect growth.
A good, cash-rich branded business at a fair price, but it needs to show that double-digit growth can last before it earns a place.
Cheap for its growth, but the growth so far has gone into stock rather than cash; wait for H1 FY27 to show positive operating cash and the margin back near 7–8%.
Store rents, interest and depreciation swallow far more than the business earns; avoid until it shows it can make money before the IPO cash runs out.
A well-run, cheap-looking distributor (about 20 times earnings), but Q1 grew volumes only 10%; I want H2 to show the promised 20% before buying.
Cheap and very profitable, but it is effectively a supplier to one retail chain; I want H1 FY27 to show 30% growth and a broader customer list first.
The plan is credible but almost all of it is promised, not delivered; I want two quarters of STEAG revenue, a better margin and foundit at breakeven first.
Cheap and cash-rich, but I want to see the card business stop shrinking and working capital come back down before buying.
A strong franchise at a fair price (about 24 times earnings), but I want two or three listed quarters showing the 30–35% growth and cash keeping up before buying.
The price is reasonable for 15% growth, but I want a strong Q2 season and better cash collection before buying.

A real business, but ₹429cr was advanced to an unnamed intermediary for a fourth ship and the latest profit leans on ₹49cr of one-off compensation; at about 90 times earnings that is too much to take on trust.
A high-quality, cash-rich franchise at a fair price, but I want to see growth return through the Delhi change and the 2027 renewals before buying.
Cheaper than its larger rival Jeena Sikho, but the profit has not yet turned into cash; I want a year of quarterly results showing it does.
At about 41 times earnings the price assumes the new lines lift margins to 25%; I want to see the new SteriPort line selling and the margin rise first.
The growth is real and the price (about 32 times earnings) is not extreme, but I want H1 FY27 to show the new plant running and profit turning back into cash.
The growth and margin are real, but I want to see operating cash turn positive and inventory fall toward the 100–110 days CRISIL expects before paying about 26 times earnings.
Cheap and cash-rich, but over a 2–4 year hold the licence end in 2030 and the falling output matter more than this year's cash; I want an extension beyond 2030 and output stabilising first.
The receivables and cash record do not fit a cash-paid clinic business, and I would need them explained and fixed first.
A well-run, cash-generating chain at about 35 times earnings with 24% guided growth; I would buy on evidence that the acquired hospitals fill up and the payer mix shifts.
A good quarry business, but at this price the governance history, the China dependence and the slow collections are not paid for.
A fast-growing recycler, but at about 27 times earnings I want to see the new copper plants lift profit per tonne and cash finally follow profit.
A real franchise with strong cash, but the price needs years of fast profit growth; I want to see the guided doubling of EBITDA and offline break-even first.
Cheap for its growth and the cash finally arrived in FY26, but it is one good cash year in a thin-margin, credit-heavy business; I want Q2 and Q3 to show the margin and collections holding.
A genuinely good business priced for many years of 40% growth; I want to see that growth hold through a few listed quarters and free cash flow turn positive, or a lower price.
A well-run, debt-free business at a fair 28 times earnings; I want Unit 3 on time and profit turning into cash before buying.
A leveraged, loss-making coal generator whose control is collateral for Vedanta Resources' borrowing, priced at about 14 times operating profit.

The contracts are good, but at well over 250 times earnings and 35 times operating profit the price already counts on 6 GW being built on time; I want to see the new firm-power plants earn before buying.

At about 10 times trailing EV/EBITDA for a low-margin commodity business with one quarter of standalone history, a Bokaro plant still waiting for clearances and a heavily indebted parent drawing fees, the risks outweigh the 4x profit plan.
A fair price (about 10 times EBITDA) for a well-run, integrated group, but profit has been flat for four years and the margin needs to break above 12% before a big four-year spending plan starts.
A fast grower with good cash conversion, but a CBI charge-sheet names the chairman and the CFO, solar is 79% of sales and about 45 times earnings already pays for this year's guided growth.
Cheap and growing, but one customer is 64% of revenue, Gujarat is 82% of orders, and only ₹5cr of ₹119cr operating profit over four years came in as cash.
Profit has not turned into cash, and the company has bet its balance sheet on a project it must now fund itself; India Ratings has turned negative.
A real market leader, but it lost money last year and management itself needs 12–15% more volume before returns look normal; I want two clean quarters of profit and falling debt first.
A small forwarder with no clear edge, shrinking volumes and profit that is not turning into cash; the low P/E does not make up for that.

Growth is real and the price low, but operating cash was −₹53cr in FY26, customers take 134 days to pay, warrants followed the CFO's 'debt only' promise, and it bought into a Thai company run by its promoters without calling it a related-party deal.

An open police case alleges bribes and over-invoicing of at least ₹44cr, and its customs status was suspended this year; with a 4% margin at about 28 times earnings, nothing here is worth that governance risk.
A real moat, but the price needs far more growth than an 8% return on capital supports, and I want the related-party purchases to shrink before buying.

The growth is real, but customers take 203 days to pay, FY26 operating cash was only ₹17cr, ICRA rated it 'not cooperating' until May 2026 and the promised KPMG audit has not happened, at about 43 times earnings.
A strong niche franchise, but at about 78 times trailing earnings the price already counts on the new businesses working; I want to see their first revenue and milestone income first.
The profit has never turned into cash, and the way the subsidiaries are being bought from the promoters puts their interests ahead of outside shareholders'.
A respectable converter, but 30 times earnings is a high price for a 4.7% margin whose profit has not turned into cash.
A well-run niche workshop, but at 93 times earnings and 23 times sales the price already assumes the jump to ₹500cr of revenue that management hopes for by FY31.
Cheap on paper, but the profit has not been turning into cash and the related-party web is large; it moves up only if FY27 delivers the guided growth and margin with positive operating cash.
A well-run niche supplier, but at about 33 times earnings the price assumes the guided 20% growth and 24–25% margin; I want to see Q2 deliver the margin rebound first.
A real niche, but only ₹92cr of ₹577cr operating profit over FY23–FY26 (16%) arrived as cash, at about 45 times earnings; it can return to the list when operating cash covers most of its profit.
A strong niche leader at about 24 times earnings, but today's profit comes near the top of a capital-spending cycle; I want to see the 20% margin and orders hold for a few quarters.
A good franchise, but the IPO is entirely the parent selling, the price is not in what I read, and I want to see its first listed results and how group dealings are handled.
A fast-growing, well-placed niche maker, but the price already assumes the FY28 target is met, and the family dealings and weak cash call for proof first.
A capable service-led switchgear firm, but at about 50 times earnings with no operating cash yet, the price assumes the new plants and margins work out.
Profitable in a wind-installation boom, but too concentrated, too new and too entangled with the family's other firm to trust through a downturn.
It looks cheap at 20 times earnings, but profit has not turned into cash for four years and the BESS plans need more money.
Too small, too new and too dependent on a few clients for a 2–4 year holding, at a price that already assumes the growth continues.
A better business than a year ago, but on reported profit the price needs far more growth than I expect, at what looks like the top of the fibre cycle.
Today's profit is real but it is peak-cycle profit, and the cash and governance record do not earn the benefit of the doubt.
A useful utility, but the price already assumes management's 30–35% growth path, and the group dealings must shrink first.
A good cancer franchise that is improving, but the price already assumes years of margin recovery.
The price roughly fits the growth I expect, but the margin is far above its rivals' and the cash has not yet followed the profit.

The cheapest of the steel-building makers, and its cash is better than the filed figures showed: its FY26 statement counted ₹120.81cr of IPO deposits as operating spending, and corrected, operating cash was about +₹90cr against ₹93cr of profit, and ₹198cr against ₹265cr over FY22–FY26 (75%). Moved up from wait on 16 October 2026; own needs H1 FY27 cash confirming it, the margin near 11% and orders recovering.

Fast, contract-backed growth at a reasonable price, but the rest of the promoter loan did not come back by the end of Q2 FY27, the condition I set for owning it; management now says the balance should be nil by March (moved from own, 16 October 2026).

The steadiest margins in the sector, and since 9 Oct 2026 a price that fits (about {need:Caplin Point Labs|17}% needed against my ~16%), with about 80% of five years' profit arriving as cash; returns are falling and receivables rising, so watch debtor days in Q2.

The price fits and drum closures earn about 40% on sales with a third of the world market, but Q1 profit was lifted by the weak rupee and investment gains, textiles earn nothing and the cash cycle is 306 days.

Defence shells lifted profit 68% and the price fits, but free cash has been negative four years, ₹219cr of bills are discounted and the swap ratio for folding in the defence subsidiary is not yet known.
A genuine niche with a 23-24% margin and net cash, but the core grew only 13% in Q1, the CFO is leaving, one customer is 17.5% of sales and the price needs about {need:Shivalik Bimetal|26}% a year.
India's dominant wire-rope maker with a 20% margin, net cash and an upgrade, but volumes have been flat for a year and the ED and CBI cases sit in the auditor's report.
Well run with Aichi Steel behind it and net cash, but volume is capped at 7-8% a year until an environmental approval arrives and a large equity raise is coming.

Debt is down and the price looks low, but sales have been flat for three years, a third of operating profit is state subsidy, half the promoter stake is pledged and ₹383cr of lender preference shares can convert into equity.

Cheap, with net cash about half its market value and 55% of Indian seamless pipe, but treasury income is 41% of pre-tax profit, the anti-dumping duty is up for renewal and a demerger leaves the cash split unclear.

A top-quality stainless tube maker with net cash and a record spool order, but the standalone business fell 30% in Q1, the Saudi plant slipped a year and the price needs far more growth than I expect.
Rare extrusion approvals, but a 5% margin, Q1 volume down about 23% and ₹23cr of yearly profit against a price that needs about {need:Welspun Specialty|35}% a year.
Capitalised in-house dies and tools equal to about half of FY26 operating profit, negative free cash every year, equity raised every year and a ₹650cr bet on circuit-board laminate it has never made.

Operating cash was −₹46cr against ₹135cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and only ₹8cr against ₹35cr in FY26 (23%); the two years since the demerger turned ₹18cr of ₹66cr of profit into cash. The price fits the ~12% growth I expect, but it returns to follow only when a full year's operating cash covers most of its profit and receivables grow slower than sales.

Strong and cheap, but its profit is not arriving as cash: operating cash was −₹6,640cr against ₹5,527cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and −₹2,811cr against ₹903cr in FY26, as money went into HAM projects. It goes back to follow only once operating cash turns positive and converts most of its profit, with orders arriving and no new legal surprise.

A growing business whose profit has not turned into cash: operating cash was −₹1,030cr against ₹1,193cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and still −₹91cr against ₹309cr in FY26. It goes back to follow once operating cash turns positive and converts most of its profit, with a clean internal-control report.

The cheapest of the steel-building makers but the weakest at turning profit into cash: ₹77cr of operating cash against ₹265cr of profit over FY22–FY26 (29%), and −₹31cr against ₹93cr in FY26. It goes back to follow once operating cash turns positive and converts most of its profit, with the margin near 11% and orders recovering.

A reliable grower, but less than half its profit has arrived as cash: ₹173cr of operating cash against ₹427cr of profit over FY22–FY26 (41%), and −₹19cr against ₹135cr in FY26. It goes back to follow once operating cash turns positive and converts most of its profit, with the tax question settled.

Operating cash was −₹164cr against ₹326cr of profit over FY22–FY26 (−₹170cr in FY26), because land buying counts as operating spending; strong bookings and a fair price, but own it only once filed operating cash turns positive and net debt stays within India Ratings' band.

Its profit does not arrive as cash: operating cash was −₹642cr against ₹7,098cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and only ₹231cr against ₹1,284cr in FY26 (18%), as stock and credit to resellers absorbed it. A well-run leader in a price-driven boom; back to follow once operating cash converts most of its profit (above ₹1,000cr a year) and the PC price boom settles.

Operating cash was −₹60cr against ₹316cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and −₹116cr against ₹202cr in FY26, as stock and borrowings ballooned. The cell plant could transform profits, but it returns to follow only once the cell line is running and operating cash turns positive.

Operating cash was −₹17cr against ₹54cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and −₹7cr against ₹28cr in FY26. Fast, profitable growth, but it returns to follow only when the half-year results show operating cash turning positive.

Its profit is not arriving as cash: operating cash was ₹18cr against ₹297cr of profit over FY23–FY26 (6%), and −₹44cr against ₹132cr of profit in FY26. It returns to follow when operating cash turns positive and covers most of its profit, with the cathode plant running.

Its profit is not arriving as cash: operating cash was −₹22cr against ₹68cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and −₹8cr against ₹26cr of profit in FY26, as stock and debt grow. Growth is slowing too, and the price needs about {need:Macfos|22–23}% a year against my ~20%. It returns to follow when operating cash turns positive and covers most of its profit.

Its profit is not arriving as cash: operating cash was ₹33cr against ₹85cr of profit over FY22–FY26 (39%), and −₹14cr against ₹41cr of profit in FY26, with ₹115cr of bills discounted off the balance sheet. Earnings should step up as the new lines fill and the price asks for about what I expect; it returns to follow when operating cash turns positive and covers most of its profit.

Its profit has not arrived as cash: −₹248cr of operating cash against ₹306cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and −₹215cr against ₹132cr in FY26 as stock piled up. A real growth story, but it leans on a memory-chip shortage that will not last for ever; it returns to follow once operating cash turns positive and covers most of its profit, with net debt back toward the ~₹300cr promised. The price is {label:GNG Electronics|full}: it needs about {need:GNG Electronics|26}% a year against my ~22%.

Its profit has not arrived as cash: −₹61cr of operating cash against ₹317cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and −₹119cr against ₹134cr in FY26 alone. An excellent business, but it returns to follow only once operating cash turns positive and covers most of its profit without more bill discounting.

Its profit is not arriving as cash: ₹152cr of operating cash against ₹395cr of profit over the five years Screener shows (FY21–FY26, FY24 not shown; 38%), and ₹2cr on ₹110cr in FY26. A strong fabricator in a reset year, with new orders taken close to historic margins; it returns to follow when operating cash converts most of its profit and the second half brings the margin back. The price needs about {need:The Anup Enginee|21}% a year against my ~18%, which is {Label:The Anup Enginee|Full}.

Its profit is not arriving as cash: operating cash was −₹76cr against ₹168cr of profit over FY24–FY26 (the three years on record), and −₹114cr in FY26 alone. The data-centre growth is real, but it returns to follow only when operating cash turns positive and converts most of its profit, with Vertiv ordering in volume.

Its profit is not arriving as cash: operating cash was −₹11cr against ₹174cr of profit over FY23–FY26 (the four years on record), and −₹2cr in FY26. A strong order book, but it depends on oilfield customers; it returns to follow when operating cash turns positive and converts most of its profit at a 30% margin.

Its profit is not yet arriving as cash: ₹74cr of operating cash against ₹156cr of profit over FY22–FY26 (47%), and FY26 converted 46%. A small, integrated wear-protection specialist that has become the preferred workshop for foreign equipment designers; it returns to own when receivables come down and operating cash covers most of its profit.

Its profit is not arriving as cash: operating cash was −₹40cr against ₹1,039cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and FY26 converted only 4% (₹13cr on ₹368cr). A strong brand, but the share price already assumes a lot of growth; it returns to follow when operating cash turns clearly positive and converts most of its profit, with the price rises still sticking.

Its profit is not arriving as cash: operating cash was −₹55cr against ₹87cr of profit over FY22–FY26, and −₹55cr on ₹43cr of profit in FY26. It is in the right part of the chain; it returns to follow when operating cash turns positive and converts most of its profit.
